messages:
Mike: Canary showed a regression for INT8 workloads this morning — p99 up ~17%, CPU usage spiked on dequant path. CI perf test failed and canary was paused.
Sara: I landed PR #3189 yesterday which changed the kernel-routing heuristic to prefer fused-dequant for short sequences. I assumed wins but maybe mixed workloads break it.
Mike: Quick perf summary from the canary run:
```
model: redwood-int8-v2
workload: mixed seq lengths (avg 42 tokens)
p50: 32ms -> 35ms (+9%)
p95: 58ms -> 66ms (+13%)
p99: 120ms -> 141ms (+17.5%)
CPU user: 42% -> 61% (hotspot in dequant)
KV cache hit: 98.1% -> 97.9% (no meaningful change)
```

Anna: If KV hit rate is stable, maybe the fused-dequant path doesn't play nicely with our kernel selection for medium sequences.
Raj: I did a quick bisect on staging -> points to commit 9f2a7c1 (merge PR #3189 by @Sara). That commit sets `prefer_fused_dequant = true` in kernel_selector for seq_len <= 32.
Sara: The microbench I ran used seq_len 8/12 only. Oops, our runtime workload has a long tail. I'll add a guard and extra microbench variants.
Mike: Flamegraphs show majority of time in `quant/dequant.cu` called from `runtime/kernel_selector` after the change. Looks like extra copies/dequant overhead for sequences where fused path triggers then falls back to KV handling.
Dev-bot: CI: perf/int8/latency FAILED on commit 9f2a7c1 — failure details: https://ci.redwood/12345
Mike: Action items: 1) hold canary (done), 2) revert 9f2a7c1 in staging to confirm regression clears, 3) add e2e perf test with mixed seq distribution, 4) follow-up PR to make fused path conditional on measured seq distribution + KV-cache-safe flag.
Sara: I'll open the revert PR and a follow-up to gate by `seq_distribution` + add KV interaction test. Also will add a note to the release checklist to run mixed-length perf harness.
Deploy-bot: Revert PR 9f2a7c1 merged to staging (deploy queued).
Mike: Once staging perf tests pass, we'll unpause the canary and continue the release. Thanks for the quick bisect/response team :thumbsup:
